subject: POC Trial: workload profile intake & success criteria - Acme Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC trial follow-up & workload intake (next steps)

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we spin up the trial environment: 

1) Success criteria (what will make this POC successful):
   - End-to-end latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 450ms for the primary inference path (interactive 512-token prompts).
   - Throughput: sustain 60 QPS of short-form inference (average prompt + completion ~ 120 tokens) for 8 hours with bursts to 200 QPS for up to 10 minutes.
   - Cost target: average token cost below $0.004/token (we'll show estimates after we confirm model/quantization choices).
   - Functional: model qualitative pass on the 25 sample prompts you provided, with no more than a 10% drop vs. your in-house baseline on critical intents.

2) Workload intake items we need (see attached workload_profile_template.xlsx):
   - Request profile: average RPS, peak RPS, typical burst duration, concurrency per user/session.
   - Token lengths: median and 95th for prompts and completions.
   - Session type: synchronous vs streaming, any long-polling or background batching.
   - Auth/region requirements and any allowed IP ranges for dedicated or private options.

3) Timeline and ownership:
   - You: complete the workload_profile_template and return by Tue, Feb 23.
   - Redwood: provision trial environment and baseline perf test plan by Fri, Feb 26.
   - Joint: kickoff POC validation week starting Mon, Mar 1.

4) Logistics:
   - I'll provision a Redwood trial cluster scoped for your expected load once we have the intake.
   - Marissa will own the integration checklist and baseline evals.

Attachments: workload_profile_template.xlsx (please fill), redwood-poc-scope.pdf (scope & security notes).

If that schedule looks good I’ll send the intake template and calendar invites.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC trial follow-up & workload intake (next steps)

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. We're aligned on the goals; a few clarifications and the preliminary numbers below: 

- We can commit to filling the workload template by EOD Tue, Feb 23.
- Preliminary traffic profile (high-level):
   * Average RPS: 18 requests/s (production baseline)
   * Peak RPS: 120 requests/s (daily peak, 10-12am PST)
   * Burst pattern: up to 220 RPS for 5-12 minutes during certain campaign spikes (roughly weekly)
   * Concurrency: typical concurrent sessions ~40, with spikes to ~140
   * Token lengths: median prompt 80 tokens; median completion 220 tokens; 95th percentile total tokens ~950

- Streaming: yes for interactive flows, but we can accept server-side chunking for the POC if that simplifies deployment.

- Security: we prefer private networking for PHI-safe endpoints; can Marissa and I sync on the options?

We'll attach the completed template with some of these numbers; Samir is looped for procurement timeline.

Best,
Jane
Jane Doe | Senior PM, Conversational AI
Acme Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC trial follow-up & workload intake (next steps)

Jane —

Appreciate the numbers — that's very helpful and matches what we discussed. A few follow-ups and an updated evaluation plan: 

- Baseline test plan (what Redwood will run):
   * Spike & soak tests to validate the 220 RPS bursts and 120 sustained peaks (30-min and 2-hr windows).
   * Latency histogram capture for median/95/99, comparing streaming vs chunked responses.
   * Cost estimate matrix across model families (4x variants), quantization profiles, and batching windows.

- POC environment: we recommend starting with a dedicated trial pool (multi-GPU) that we can scale with burst capacity. If you need PHI isolation, we can provide Redwood Private (VPC) trial — Marissa will reach out to coordinate network details and an NDA addendum if required.

- Success criteria (tightening):
   1) 95th pctl latency <= 450ms for interactive happy path at 120 RPS sustained.
   2) No more than 2% error rate for inference requests during 220 RPS bursts.
   3) Model quality: pass >= 22/25 of your sample prompts per the rubric we'll share.

Next steps I’ll take:
   - Provision trial infra once the filled template is in (ETA 48-72h after receipt).
   - Share perf baseline runbook and the rubric by end of day Thu, Feb 25.

Marissa: can you own the network checklist and confirm whether the VPC trial requires any account-level approvals from Acme?

Thanks — looking forward to the intake file.

-Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
